name: Hsp90 (Hsp82) positions 582–590, growth over 21 generations (EMPIRIC)
description: Every codon at nine positions of yeast Hsp90 (Hsp82), made with NNN codons and inserted by cassette ligation, transformed into yeast whose own Hsp90 is temperature-sensitive (G170D). At 36 °C that copy is inactive, so growth depends on the variant. Sampled at eight times, 0 to 21 wild-type generations, in one replicate. MaveDB names each codon variant on its own row; MaveScape reads them at the protein level, each amino-acid substitution's codons combined.

source.citation: Hietpas RT, Jensen JD, Bolon DNA. Experimental illumination of a fitness landscape. PNAS 2011;108:7896–7901. doi:10.1073/pnas.1016024108

readout.phenotype: Growth of yeast whose only active Hsp90 carries the variant (36 °C, the temperature-sensitive copy inactivated)

why.nonsense: Hsp90 is essential in yeast, and a stop at any of these positions truncates it.

notes: MaveDB's protein column names the wild type's nine copies (one per position) as synonymous changes; MaveScape names each row from its nucleotide name instead, and reads the copies once.
